databaseUrl.title: Build your Postgres connection URL
databaseUrl.step1: Find the host, port, database name, user and password — in your hosting provider's dashboard (look for "connection string"), or from your local setup.
databaseUrl.step2: Combine them as postgresql://user:password@host:5432/database. Encode special characters in the password (for example @ becomes %40).
databaseUrl.step3: Prefer a database user with read-only permissions for the agent.

apiKey.title: Get a Brave Search API key
apiKey.step1: Sign in to the Brave Search API dashboard.
apiKey.step2: Subscribe to a plan — the free plan is enough to start.
apiKey.step3: Open API Keys, create a key, and copy it.

apiKey.title: Get a Tavily API key
apiKey.step1: Sign in or create a free account at Tavily.
apiKey.step2: Your default API key is on the overview page — copy it (it starts with tvly-).

apiKey.title: Get an Exa API key
apiKey.step1: Sign in to the Exa dashboard.
apiKey.step2: Open API Keys, create a key, and copy it.

apiKey.title: Get a Firecrawl API key
apiKey.step1: Sign in or sign up at Firecrawl.
apiKey.step2: Open API Keys and copy your key (it starts with fc-).

apiKey.title: Get a Context7 API key
apiKey.step1: Sign in to the Context7 dashboard.
apiKey.step2: Create an API key and copy it.

token.title: Get a Notion integration secret
token.step1: Open Notion's integrations page and create a new internal integration in your workspace.
token.step2: Copy its Internal Integration Secret (it starts with ntn_).
token.step3: In Notion, open each page or database the agent should see, choose ••• → Connections, and add your integration. It cannot see anything you have not shared.

token.title: Create an Airtable personal access token
token.step1: Open the token creation page and name the token.
token.step2: Add the scopes schema.bases:read and data.records:read — and data.records:write if the agent should edit.
token.step3: Choose which bases it can access, create it, and copy the token (it starts with pat).

apiToken.title: Create an Atlassian API token
apiToken.step1: Open your Atlassian account's API tokens page and choose Create API token.
apiToken.step2: Name it, pick an expiry, and copy the token — it is shown only once.
apiToken.step3: Use the email you sign in with, and your site URL such as https://your-team.atlassian.net.

token.title: Create a Figma personal access token
token.step1: In Figma, open your account menu → Settings → Security.
token.step2: Under Personal access tokens, generate a new token with read access to file content.
token.step3: Copy it right away — Figma shows it only once.

token.title: Create a GitHub personal access token
token.step1: Open GitHub's new fine-grained token page and name the token.
token.step2: Choose the repositories, then grant what the agent needs — for example Contents, Issues and Pull requests (read, or read and write).
token.step3: Generate the token and copy it (it starts with github_pat_).

token.title: Create a Sentry user auth token
token.step1: Open Sentry → User settings → Personal Tokens.
token.step2: Create a token with at least org:read, project:read and event:read.
token.step3: Copy the token — it is shown only once.

token.title: Create a Supabase access token
token.step1: Open your Supabase account's Access Tokens page and generate a new token.
token.step2: Name it and copy it (it starts with sbp_).
